title: Vue 3 Essentials: Composition API from Scratch
summary: Build reactive interfaces with script setup, refs, computed values and composables.
description: Start from zero and finish with a production-ready single page application. This course walks through the reactivity system, component composition, and the patterns professional teams rely on every day. You will build three projects, each one introducing a new slice of the framework.
outcomes: Create components with the script setup syntax
Manage reactive state with ref, reactive and computed
Extract reusable logic into composables
Handle forms, events and two-way binding confidently

lessons.title: Props, emits and the data flow contract

title: Responsive and Accessible Interface Design
summary: Design layouts that work on every screen and for every user, not just the average one.
description: Accessibility is not a checklist you bolt on at the end. This course teaches a mobile-first workflow where semantics, colour contrast and keyboard support are decisions you make while you draw the first box, using modern CSS layout as the foundation.
outcomes: Apply a mobile-first CSS methodology
Meet WCAG AA contrast and focus requirements
Build layouts with Grid and Flexbox
Audit an interface with a screen reader

lessons.title: Grid, Flexbox and when to use which

title: Asynchronous JavaScript in Depth
summary: Promises, async/await, error boundaries and the event loop, explained properly.
description: Most bugs in modern frontends are timing bugs. This course goes underneath the syntax to the event loop itself, then rebuilds your mental model of promises, cancellation, retries and race conditions so that asynchronous code stops being a source of surprise.
outcomes: Explain the event loop, microtasks and macrotasks
Write robust async/await with real error handling
Cancel in-flight requests with AbortController
Design retry and loading state strategies

title: Data Visualisation for the Web
summary: Turn raw numbers into charts that inform rather than decorate.
description: A practical tour of encoding data into visual form. You will learn which chart earns its place for which question, how to build charts directly in SVG without a heavy library, and how to keep them readable for colour-blind users and on small screens.
outcomes: Choose the right chart for the question being asked
Build charts in raw SVG with scales you control
Design accessible, colour-blind safe palettes
Make visualisations responsive

lessons.title: Colour that survives a colour-blind check

title: Client-Side State Management Patterns
summary: Know when state belongs in a component, a composable, or a global store.
description: Global stores are frequently reached for too early and cause more coupling than they remove. This course gives you a decision framework for placing state, then goes deep on store design, derived state, persistence and testing.
outcomes: Decide where a piece of state should live
Design Pinia stores with clear boundaries
Derive state instead of duplicating it
Persist and rehydrate state safely

lessons.title: A decision tree for state placement
Derived state and the duplication trap

title: UX Research Fundamentals
summary: Ask better questions, run useful sessions, and turn findings into decisions.
description: Research fails when it produces opinions instead of evidence. Learn to plan a study, recruit honestly, run interviews and usability sessions without leading participants, and synthesise what you hear into something a product team can act on.
outcomes: Write research questions that can be answered
Run interviews without leading the participant
Synthesise notes into themes and insights
Communicate findings to stakeholders

lessons.title: What research can and cannot tell you

title: Consuming REST APIs Like a Professional
summary: Contracts, caching, pagination and failure, the parts tutorials skip.
description: Fetching data is easy on the happy path. This short, dense course covers the rest: HTTP semantics, pagination strategies, optimistic updates, caching, and designing a data layer that degrades gracefully when the network does not cooperate.
outcomes: Read and honour an HTTP API contract
Handle pagination and partial data
Implement caching and optimistic updates
Degrade gracefully on network failure

title: Building a Developer Portfolio That Gets Replies
summary: Present your work the way hiring teams actually read it.
description: A portfolio is a communication problem, not a design problem. Learn to choose which projects to show, write case studies that explain your reasoning, and structure a site that a reviewer can scan in ninety seconds.
outcomes: Select projects that demonstrate range
Write a case study with a clear decision narrative
Structure a portfolio for fast scanning
Prepare for the walkthrough interview

title: Testing Frontend Applications
summary: Write tests that catch real regressions instead of restating the implementation.
description: A test suite is only valuable if it fails for the right reasons. This course covers the testing pyramid in a component world, choosing what to assert, testing asynchronous UI, and wiring the whole thing into continuous integration.
outcomes: Decide what is worth testing
Test components through user-visible behaviour
Handle async UI in tests reliably
Run the suite in CI on every push

title: Product Analytics for Builders
summary: Instrument a product so the numbers answer the question you actually asked.
description: Learn to define events before you fire them, avoid vanity metrics, build a funnel that reflects real user intent, and read a cohort chart without fooling yourself.
outcomes: Define an event taxonomy up front
Distinguish signal metrics from vanity metrics
Build and read a conversion funnel
Interpret retention cohorts honestly

title: TypeScript for Vue Developers
summary: Type your props, emits, stores and API responses without fighting the compiler.
description: TypeScript pays off in a component codebase when the types describe your contracts rather than your data structures. This course focuses on the Vue-specific patterns: typed props and emits, generic components, typed stores, and narrowing API responses at the boundary.
outcomes: Type props, emits and slots precisely
Write generic, reusable components
Type Pinia stores and composables
Validate and narrow API responses

title: Interface Motion and Micro-interactions
summary: Motion that explains what changed, and respects people who prefer none.
description: Good motion is functional: it shows where an element came from, confirms an action, and covers a wait. Learn easing, duration and choreography, plus how to honour prefers-reduced-motion without gutting the experience.
outcomes: Use motion to explain state change
Pick durations and easing curves deliberately
Choreograph multi-element transitions
Respect prefers-reduced-motion

lessons.title: Motion with a job to do
Reduced motion as a first-class path
